correctness.rationale: The Fraïssé extension property bijects types with ideal/filter profiles. One-sided profiles are \(2J-1\), and mixed profiles are complete-cross-edge nonempty bipartite subset pairs. The exact finite expectation sums follow by independent-edge indicators. A Markov bound makes excess ideals negligible on the \(2^n\) scale. Each fixed small-side stratum W_{n,k} has asymptotic mean α^k/k! and variance O(\(4^n n^{-1/2}\)), using the exact shared-row covariance. A three-range entropy bound plus a both-sides-macroscopic estimate controls the infinite small-side tail, justifying quenched limits and conditional total-variation Poisson fringes. The executable directly enumerates all 1, 2, 3 balanced-shore random graphs with exact rational mean checks, independently checks type closures, and compares larger exact expectations; finite tests are not used as proofs.

Both are mathematically adjacent but do not yield the asserted concentration and conditional law.

originality.rationale: The ideal/filter profile, height-two type count via complementary independent sets, and bipartite hard-core techniques are known. Full-text comparisons locate deterministic 1-type sensitivity, weak-order averages, regular-expander hard-core approximation, and maximum biclique-size results, none implying the stated logarithmic-window *quenched* type-count constant together with a uniform-type zero-truncated Poisson fringe law. A distinct earlier random-base calculation applies only to \(n^2q\) bounded and gives \(T/4^n\), not the present q=(2 log n+t)/n, \(T/\(2^n\)\) regime. Stronger unindexed hard-core asymptotics remain a real priority risk; PASS is best-knowledge, not a universal uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently formulated sparse random bipartite hard-core partition-function result might imply the present quenched constant and minority-fringe law.
Some literature on random independent-set polymer phase coexistence was identifiable only through search abstracts; no universal novelty proof is possible.
The novelty of the exact finite expectations is not claimed; it is the quenched critical limit and conditional profile that require priority validation.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the sharp nontrivial critical transition of the *fraction* of extensions situated between old parameters, not just their expected count, on a natural random family in homogeneous model theory. It yields both the explicit crossover \(\tanh(e^{-t/2}/2)\) and the zero-truncated Poisson shape of a uniformly sampled mixed type, clarifying the transition from one-sided to genuinely two-sided extensions. The exact finite sums and the exhaustive proof identify the mechanism and limiting scope, not merely a numerical fit.
